reading:
NTT's US data center business operates as NTT DATA Global Data Centers Americas, the current name for what was formerly RagingWire Data Centers, under the umbrella of NTT DATA Group and its parent, Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corporation, a Japanese public company listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange and also traded in the US through an ADR. As a foreign private issuer, it is not an SEC 10-K filer, so no US SEC CIK applies to this entry.

The operator's own site states seven US data center campuses with named capacity figures: Ashburn, Virginia at 224 megawatts, Chicago, Illinois at more than 200 megawatts, Dallas, Texas at 160 megawatts, Hillsboro, Oregon at 126 megawatts, Phoenix, Arizona at 240 megawatts, and a combined Sacramento and Santa Clara, California figure of 68 megawatts. The site totals these seven US campuses at approximately 1,118 megawatts or more of capacity, among the largest single capacity figures disclosed by any operator in this registry so far, ahead of the round figures given by CyrusOne and Flexential.

The registry here tracks 25 NTT facilities across six states, California, Illinois, Oregon, Texas, Virginia, and Washington, fewer discrete rows than the seven-campus structure NTT describes, consistent with NTT's campus model of multiple buildings clustered per named location rather than one row per campus. This capacity concentration in Ashburn and Phoenix, both markets already carrying heavy AWS, Google, and Meta buildout tracked elsewhere in this registry, reinforces the pattern of hyperscaler-adjacent colocation demand clustering in the same power-constrained metro corridors.
